name: Washington County

actions.title: HB 4084 Enterprise Zone Moratorium — Pre-Deadline Application Rush
actions.summary: Oregon's 2026 Legislature passed HB 4084 placing a moratorium on new data center Enterprise Zone tax-break applications effective June 6, 2026, triggering a rush of 17 applications in Hillsboro before the deadline.

actions.title: Hillsboro City Councilor Moratorium Petition
actions.summary: Hillsboro City Councilor Kipperlyn Sinclair launched a public petition calling for a temporary local moratorium on new data center development to allow study of economic, environmental, and energy impacts.

actions.title: Hillsboro City Council Data Center Work Sessions
actions.summary: Hillsboro City Council held public work sessions on June 2 and 9, 2026 to evaluate data center impacts and explore potential changes to the city's land use code, including requiring environmental review.

actions.title: Lawsuit to Block 17 Data Center Enterprise Zone Agreements
actions.summary: 1000 Friends of Oregon, Oregon Education Association, Tax Fairness Oregon, and Tualatin Riverkeepers filed suit in Washington County Circuit Court alleging Hillsboro and the county improperly approved 17 data center Enterprise Zone tax breaks without required public notice.

actions.title: Oregon PUC POWER Act Order — PGE Data Center Rate Increase
actions.summary: Oregon's Public Utility Commission issued an order implementing the POWER Act, approving a 29% rate increase for data centers served by Portland General Electric and requiring data centers to pay for generation and transmission infrastructure they cause to be built.

contextBlurb: Washington County — centered on Hillsboro — is Oregon's largest data center market, home to 21 data centers on 436 acres with over $11.6 billion in active enterprise zone investments. Community opposition surged in early 2026, culminating in a major public rally in May, a city council moratorium petition, and a landmark lawsuit challenging 17 last-minute tax-break agreements. The Oregon Legislature's HB 4084 moratorium on Enterprise Zone incentives for data centers (effective June 6, 2026) and the PUC's POWER Act rate order have made Washington County the epicenter of Oregon's data center policy battles.

name: Morrow County

actions.title: Morrow County Commission Emergency Declaration — Nitrate Groundwater Contamination
actions.summary: The Morrow County Commission declared a public health emergency over nitrate contamination of the Lower Umatilla Basin groundwater, which residents and advocates linked in part to data center cooling water discharges.

actions.title: Amazon Data Services $20.5M Nitrate Groundwater Settlement
actions.summary: A class-action settlement requiring Amazon to pay $20.5 million for alleged contribution to nitrate groundwater contamination in the Lower Umatilla Basin Groundwater Management Area spanning Morrow and Umatilla counties was filed for court approval.

actions.title: Oregon Nitrate Reduction Plan — DEQ Wastewater Permit Modernization
actions.summary: Oregon DEQ began implementing the Oregon Nitrate Reduction Plan, modernizing wastewater permits to limit nitrogen application to soil from data centers and other industrial users in Morrow County, with enforcement authority taking effect in 2026.

contextBlurb: Morrow County hosts roughly 13 Amazon data centers at the Port of Morrow along with other hyperscale operators, drawn by cheap hydropower and Columbia River water access. The county declared a groundwater emergency over nitrate contamination affecting at least 634 domestic wells in the Lower Umatilla Basin, a crisis that litigation tied in part to data center cooling water discharges. Amazon's $20.5 million settlement in March 2026 — the first of its kind nationally — triggered intensified scrutiny of data center siting and water practices across the region.

name: Umatilla County

actions.title: Pearson v. Port of Morrow — Class Action Including Umatilla County Residents
actions.summary: Residents of Morrow and Umatilla counties sued the Port of Morrow and multiple industrial defendants — including Amazon data centers — alleging nitrate contamination of the Lower Umatilla Basin Groundwater Management Area, seeking class-action status for all affected well users.

contextBlurb: Umatilla County shares the Lower Umatilla Basin Groundwater Management Area with Morrow County, a 562-square-mile zone that is the sole water source for approximately 45,000 residents. Data center cooling operations at the Port of Morrow have been alleged in ongoing litigation to have worsened decades-long nitrate contamination affecting thousands of private wells. The Amazon settlement and continuing suit against remaining defendants are shaping local and state policy on data center water use across the Columbia Basin.
